facts: long a Desktop tab may hold its session with nothing running before the app gives the slot back.

Ending early is not a forfeit: the server re-stamps `session_units` to the fraction actually elapsed (`buildAdmitStampStatement`), so this REFUNDS the unused window and the next send re-admits on the same instance id. Getting it wrong costs one extra admission, not a session.

Ten minutes is measured against reading a long answer and typing the next prompt. Only a turn keeps the clock alive, scrolling and typing are invisible to the server half, so it is deliberately several times longer than it would need to be if it could see the user.

ai.title: PostHog exception budget caps billed exceptions per process
ai.summary: A new `exception-budget.ts` module installs a per-process `before_send` filter in `createPostHogClient` that suppresses repeated `$exception` events, so a client stuck in a retry loop no longer bills one exception per iteration forever. The filter keeps the first sighting of each distinct error keyed by type and message (truncated to 300 chars), then reports only the 1st, 10th, 100th, 1000th occurrence and stamps the true count onto `$exception_occurrence`, capping distinct fingerprints at `MAX_DISTINCT_FINGERPRINTS` (200).
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/util/exception-budget.ts` defines `createExceptionBeforeSend`, `MAX_DISTINCT_FINGERPRINTS = 200`, `ExceptionBudgetEvent`, and `ExceptionBeforeSend`; `common/src/analytics-core.ts` now passes `before_send: createExceptionBeforeSend()` into every PostHog client inside `createPostHogClient`.
